questions.q: Why does the summary say shoppers hold more power than they used to?
a: They can compare prices and reviews instantly
They have far more money to spend than before
They trust advertising more than in the past
They prefer buying only from local stores
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes checking a price comparison on a phone before ordering the same item for less online.

questions.q: Why do millennials prefer using products over owning them, according to the summary?
a: They want the benefits without the burdens of ownership
They cannot afford to use any products at all
They distrust every sharing platform
They prefer collecting things for status
questions.why: Lesson 2 uses car sharing as an example of getting the benefit without insurance and maintenance.

questions.q: What does the summary say is happening to middle-class consumption in Asian countries?
a: It is rising as incomes grow
It is falling sharply
It has already peaked
It is limited to luxury goods
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Asian middle-class spending is climbing toward levels the West reached years ago.

questions.q: Why does the summary say keeping customers happy matters so much?
a: Replacing a lost customer costs far more than keeping one
Happy customers always spend more per visit
Loyal customers never ask for discounts
New customers are easier to find than old ones
questions.why: Lesson 3 says acquiring a new customer costs 10 to 15 times more than retaining an existing one.

questions.q: Which customer experience does the summary call the hardest but best to pull off?
a: Making customers feel special
Offering the lowest prices
Delivering as fast as possible
Sending weekly discount coupons
questions.why: Lesson 3 lists cheap prices as a weak option and feeling special as the hardest but most powerful.
